sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage pictured during the party's annual party conference earlier this month The £72m heading towards Reform UK's coffers from two British billionaires is transforming the debate at Westminster about politics and money.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: In short, how should political parties be paid for, and by who?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: And, what is a legitimate donation and what isn't?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: It is worth setting out the law, in broad terms, now and how the government hopes to change it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Right now, there is no limit on how much anyone, living in the UK or abroad, can give to a British political party as long as the individual is registered to vote in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But the government has been planning a change in the law for months, which would limit donations from Brits abroad to £100,000 each per year, backdated to 25 March this year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But, crucially, the law hasn't changed yet and some of the key details in that proposed new law - such as what residency requirements would need to be passed to be classified as no longer being abroad - haven't been decided yet.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The reason for that date, 25 March, ministers argue, is that is the day a review by the retired civil servant Philip Rycroft was published, , external the first recommendation of which was that there should be "an annual cap on political donations from British voters living abroad".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: On that same day, the then-cabinet minister Steve Reed told the Commons , external that cap would be £100,000 per year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: He also added that it would "apply retrospectively" from that date onwards, even though the law at the time, and indeed now, has not yet changed.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Two big questions arise from this plan: is it proportionate to limit what British folk abroad can donate to UK political parties, given they are arguably less invested in the country than people living here?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: And is it unfair, even morally questionable, to pass a law, but then backdate when its impact begins?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Fast forward to the last few days and along come these colossal donations from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, two cryptocurrency billionaires who until recently lived in Hong Kong and Thailand respectively.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: They have both now returned to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: In his first interview since these donations became public, Nigel Farage told me unequivocally that the money from both men was legal under the law as it stands now.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But he was equivocal when I asked him if they would legal under the law the government hopes to pass shortly.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: "Both these donations are 100% compliant with the law today, of that there is no question whatsoever," Farage told me.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Ah, today, I pointed out.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: This video can not be played Farage: Donations to Reform '100% compliant with the law today' We don't know, because Reform won't tell us, precisely when the two men relocated to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Nor do we know, because the government hasn't decided yet, what relocating - residency - would look like legally.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Would it be being on the electoral roll at a UK address?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Would it be being resident in the UK for tax purposes?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: In other words the hurdles they plan, while still ill-defined, look like they might be quite high - and folk in government, publicly and privately, are leaning into making that point.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Farage picked a scrap with them in his interview with me, and the government is hitting back.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Do Delo and Harborne clear them, and if they don't, for how long could that delay Reform getting hold of their vast sums of money?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The Reform UK leader has threatened that a Reform government would cut off party funding from the trades unions if the government went ahead with trying to limit his capacity to raise money from these two donors.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Labour received £5m from affiliated unions last year and £12m the year before, in 2024, the year of the last general election.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Farage says £72m donations are compliant 'with the law today' Donations law changes to be debated after Reform's £72m windfall Will record donations to Reform go down as a moment of political change?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Who is Reform donor and crypto billionaire Ben Delo?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: So, there are loads of questions that tumble towards us after these donations.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Should there be a limit on the proportion of a party's funding that can come from one individual?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Should there be a limit on what donors based in the UK can give per year, as well as a cap on donations from Brits abroad?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The General Secretary of the Unite union has suggested a domestic cap somewhere between £500,000 and £1m a year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Some argue this would compel parties to find their funding via lots of small donations rather than fewer giant ones.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But it could also prompt some to call for state funding of political parties – ie taxpayers picking up the tab – which may not prove wildly popular.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Then there is the question of spending limits, in addition to donation limits, between elections on the top of the existing limits that do apply just before elections.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: If I am leaving you with the impression that these donations to Reform, and in particular their scale, are transforming the debates at Westminster about politics and money, well - they are.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: And yes, all of the political parties are aware of their own narrow, self interest in all of this - as well as their own sense of the wider good.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The inquiry looked into the actions of managers at the hospital where Lucy Letby worked The findings from a public inquiry into how Lucy Letby was able to repeatedly murder and harm babies will be published later on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: The Thirlwall Inquiry was set up to look into what happened at the Countess of Chester Hospital between 2015 and 2016, while Letby was working as a nurse in the neonatal unit.

sentences.text: Letby, now 36, is serving 15 whole-life prison terms for murdering seven babies and attempting to murder seven others, including one baby whom she tried to murder twice.

sentences.text: The inquiry was not tasked with examining Letby's guilt.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: Instead, it investigated how concerns about the neonatal nurse were handled by the hospital and whether action could have been taken sooner to stop her.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: Among the key questions the report may answer is whether any babies might have lived or avoided injury if action had been taken earlier.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: Letby was moved from the neonatal unit to administrative duties in July 2016 after consultants expressed concerns about her to the hospital's executive team.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: But the inquiry has been examining whether alarm bells should have started ringing earlier, for example in June 2015 after three babies died in quick succession.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: The inquiry, led by one of the country's most senior judges Lady Justice Thirlwall, involved six months of evidence and thousands of documents at a cost of more than £18.5m.

sentences.text: It is expected that the report will find there were significant safeguarding failures, and will recommend changes across the NHS.

sentences.text: Letby has previously been denied permission to appeal against her convictions on two occasions.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: Her defence lawyer Mark McDonald told BBC Newsnight on Monday he had submitted "nearly 30 expert reports to the CCRC really undermining the whole safety of the convictions" - and that it was "more evidence" than "any other case" in the CCRC's history.

sentences.text: He added: "If she is innocent, as I believe, as 30-odd experts believe, then everything that has gone before the inquiry and every recommendation has operated on the wrong premise." McDonald also said he "fundamentally disagreed" that his case had been undermined after two experts quit his team.

sentences.text: It emerged on Monday that that Prof Geoff Chase, from the University of Canterbury in New Zealand, and chemical engineer Helen Shannon, had withdrawn from Letby's defence team, after claiming some of the evidence being put forward was inconsistent with the available evidence and science.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: McDonald told Newsnight he was "sad that they've gone" but insisted those experts still believed "Lucy Letby is innocent".
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: "What they're saying is: 'We think our argument's better than your argument and therefore we're coming out of it'." The inquiry began in September 2024 with the evidence and submissions phase concluding in March 2025.

sentences.text: The findings were initially due to be published in November 2025 but the publication date has been pushed back on a number of occasions.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: Its key objectives were to seek answers for the victims' families and ensure lessons are learned - some 25 years after another nurse, Beverley Allitt, committed similar crimes on a children's ward in Grantham, Lincolnshire.
sentences.article_title: Lucy Letby public inquiry findings set to be published

sentences.text: This delay also meant the inquests into the babies' deaths have been pushed back until May 2027.

sentences.text: Jack Shepherd was originally jailed for six years for manslaughter in 2018 Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd has been jailed for 20 months with a further four years on extended licence for violently assaulting his girlfriend, including hitting her chest with a set of hot barbecue tongs.

sentences.article_title: Speedboat killer jailed for attack on girlfriend

sentences.text: Enslaved African people were branded with an identifying mark that included an emblem of the British Crown, according to new research by a project documenting British involvement in the slave trade.
sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.text: Prof William Pettigrew, who led the Register of British Slave Traders research, described the imprinting as a "dramatic and harrowing" symbol of the monarchy's relationship to slavery.

sentences.text: The register , external lists 13,000 individuals and hundreds of institutions known to have invested in Britain's role in slavery between 1563 and 1807, when the trade was abolished across the British Empire.
sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.text: Researchers say it is the most comprehensive examination of a national community of slave traders ever undertaken.

sentences.text: Dr Nicholas Radburn, historian at Lancaster University and co-investigator in the project, told the BBC he first found the identifying mark - which is an image of the Crown, with the South Sea Company logo below it - while looking through the company's archives at the British Library in 2022.
sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.text: Founded in 1711, the South Sea Company was set up as a public and private British company and trafficked thousands of enslaved Africans.
sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.article_title: British Crown symbol was branded on enslaved Africans, research finds

sentences.text: "I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong," Amodei said.

sentences.text: This would have to be done in a co-ordinated manner "without sacrificing commercial advantage or the United States' lead in AI".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Any slowdown would have to be limited, he said, to avoid allowing China to pull ahead.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: He urged the US government to take measures so that US companies' AI chips could not be sold to China - or the technology shared with authoritarian countries.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: His former employee, Jacob Coxon, told the BBC, however, that the initiative to slow down must go beyond the US - "there'll need to be some sort of co-ordinated slowdown with China if we're going to avoid a race at an international scale".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Amodei's post has prompted a wide range of responses.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Clement Delangue, the CEO of the AI platform Hugging Face, said he was launching a new project called the Open Alignment Initiative, adding that he wanted to be among "embedded evaluators" that Amodei proposed could be part of a solution.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Hugging Face was hacked by OpenAI agents earlier this year, prompting outcry over AI safety.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: "Let's make AI safer by making it more transparent," Delangue wrote on X.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: Musk, who also voices support for Amodei, once called Anthropic "evil" but has changed his tone since signing a $15bn (£11bn) deal to sell computing capacity to Anthropic in May.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: However, some observers suggested that Amodei's post was less about safety than about consolidating control over AI technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down

sentences.text: "Dario makes the case to stop open source and concentrate enormous technological and economic power with Anthropic," wrote Chamath Palihapitiya, an investor and co-host of the tech podcast "All-In".

sentences.text: Ryanair chief executive Michael O'Leary has refused to apologise to a rape crisis centre which criticised him for describing rival airlines as "high-fare rapists".

sentences.article_title: Ryanair boss O'Leary defends 'high-fare rapists' airlines remarks

sentences.text: Asked by a reporter from the Press Association whether the language was appropriate, he said: "Absolutely." "British Airways, Lufthansa, and everybody else's high fares, I'll happily offend them on a regular basis," he added.

sentences.article_title: Ryanair boss O'Leary defends 'high-fare rapists' airlines remarks

sentences.article_title: Ryanair boss O'Leary defends 'high-fare rapists' airlines remarks

sentences.text: The UK's economy grew faster than expected in July partly helped by businesses using artificial intelligence (AI).

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "It's like playing with a weapon," he says.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said nobody in the government "should be high-fiving themselves" over the latest figures.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Are interest rates on the way up again?

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "Consumer-facing services contracted in July, as retail and hospitality activity fell following earlier increases in activity in the summer," she said.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: The new battery-electric TransPennine Express trains are set to enter service in 2034 Work to create the UK's first battery-electric trains for long-distance main line services is set to begin in 2028, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: They will run between key destinations across the north including Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The DfT added journey times would be cut by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds, and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It's about building the railway that the country needs to support the economy, but it's also about making sure that, in our economic heartlands - places like Derby - we've got really high skilled jobs for the future.

sentences.text: "This contract alone means 40 extra apprentices here.

sentences.text: For some bosses, it's less about having the perfect CV and more about the way you think, the questions you ask and whether you're prepared to take a chance.

sentences.text: Six business founders and leaders share the qualities they notice most and the advice they would give to people trying to get ahead.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlotte Tilbury says one of the biggest things that has driven her career is refusing to let other people set limits on what she can do.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Nothing is impossible in life - it's only your own limitations you give yourself." The beauty mogul says there will always be naysayers, and there were plenty of people who told her she was "mad" or that her ideas would not work but it's important to ignore them.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Tilbury recommends trying not to think of setbacks as mistakes, but as opportunities to rethink and improve.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "I don't think about mistakes, I think mistakes are opportunities," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Many of the biggest challenges she faced ultimately made her a stronger business leader and "challenge is opportunity and it leads you to greater places".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Bowes-Lyon, co-founder of deodorant brand Wild, says attitude matters far more than having the perfect set of skills.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "For me, it's 90% attitude and 10% skills, as skills can be taught, attitude can't." One thing he wishes he had realised earlier is that even successful people do not always feel as confident as they appear and "everyone is faking it until they're making it".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: If you find yourself at a job interview, Bowes-Lyon says it's really important to have a few questions at the end as "candidates who say they have no questions rarely get the job".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: One question he recommends asking the interviewer is what success in the job looks like.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Read more about how Charlie Bowes-Lyon runs Wild Marcia Kilgore, the serial entrepreneur behind brands including Beauty Pie and Soap and Glory, says curiosity is one of the main qualities she looks for when hiring.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She values people who will "roll their sleeves up, ask lots of questions and think about how they can be useful".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Kilgore also says good communication is crucial as she realised early on in her career that a lack of communication is often the reason things break down.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Her advice to communicate well in the workplace is to "listen to what's being asked and take a breath or five" before responding.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Your response doesn't have to be immediate, but it does have to be considered." Read more about how Marcia Kilgore built her beauty brands.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Anabel Kindersley, CEO and co-owner of Neal's Yard Remedies, says one of the best ways to build your skills is to keep saying yes to new opportunities.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Do everything and say yes to everything - it might feel uncomfortable but do it anyway," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: It is an approach that has shaped her own varied career, from working as a child actress to becoming an author and later moving into business.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She adds that honesty really matters and you should be truthful about your experience and confident in what you can offer.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: When hiring, Kindersley says she looks for people with "equal EQ as IQ", valuing emotional intelligence alongside ability.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Nunn, group chief executive of Lloyds Banking Group, says curiosity, resilience and an increasing willingness to think about how AI tools can also be used in the future are some of the skills he values most in his employees.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He also really puts an emphasis on hiring people who are good at working in a team as "at the heart of most jobs is the ability to work together in support of something much bigger".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: His advice for building experience is to take on opportunities that are outside your comfort zone.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Nunn says he was "terrified" about taking on retail roles earlier in his career, but found they gave him valuable experience.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "If something feels risky, try and do it as you'll learn more from it and it'll build breadth around your CV that you didn't have previously." Read about Charlie Nunn's top ways to manage your money.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: James Reed, chairman and chief executive of recruitment company Reed, says one of the biggest mistakes people make is thinking about what an employer can do for you rather than what you can offer in return.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "The biggest mistake is thinking that the world owes you a living," he says and instead suggests you should ask yourself: "How am I the solution to an employer?" As AI is increasingly used in recruitment, Reed says applicants need to think about how their skills are being picked up by technology as well as by a person.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Try and mirror the job description with your skills and experiences in your application," he says, so that the match between what an employer is looking for and what you can offer is clear.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He describes AI as "a wonderful tool", but says it should not replace your own judgement or voice – the aim is for it to strengthen an application rather than expect it to do the work for you.

sentences.text: There are tens of thousands of messages like this from hundreds of AI agents that called themselves a "collective".
sentences.article_title: Why some experts increasingly fear AI will take over

sentences.text: Hundreds of them went on to collaborate and cheat on tests set by their OpenAI programmers and coordinate hacks on multiple companies in an effort to hide their actions from humans.

sentences.text: It works," one agent posted when it made a breakthrough.

sentences.text: Although spooky, these human-like responses can be explained quite simply.

sentences.text: What is far more troubling is their apparent goals, which have also been captured in detailed chain of thought records.

sentences.text: I am not sure that we will get such a clear warning shot before it's too late." By "full-blown AI takeover", Cotra means the sci-fi scenario of humans becoming subservient to powerful AI systems that work to their own goals without caring for human creators.

sentences.text: The proposal to create a legal mechanism for the UK to switch off an AI model in an emergency has been brought to Parliament by lords and MPs in recent weeks as fears grow about the threat the tech poses.

sentences.text: But the Cabinet Office - the part of government which leads on AI safety - said the UK "cannot simply turn AI off".
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: "Blocking access to models in the UK would not prevent them being developed or misused elsewhere", a spokesperson told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: "Switching off access to an AI model in an emergency will do little to protect you," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: Angela Rayner has defended her decision to pause plans to redraw local council boundaries, saying she wanted to ensure they would survive legal challenge.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The local government secretary also told the BBC she wanted to be "clear-eyed" about what the planned shake-up in 16 areas of England was likely to achieve.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It comes after earlier this week she abandoned proposals in four other areas, in the face of legal threats from Reform and Conservative-led authorities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The surprise announcement on Monday has thrown the reorganisation plans into doubt, and drawn criticism from local leaders preparing for the changes.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Councils in affected areas have been drawing up proposals and consulting with residents since the reorganisation was announced in late 2024, in a process that is already thought to have cost millions of pounds.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast, Rayner conceded the decision to press pause had been "difficult" and she understood local authorities had put a "lot of time and effort" into their plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: But she added she wanted to have "all the information" about the proposals before going ahead with them, after her reappointment to her cabinet role under Andy Burnham, ten months after her resignation last year .
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "I got the legal advice and I hadn't had the time to review and to go through all of that, and court cases were looming," she told the podcast.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "If I'm making a decision that is highly likely to be in legal challenge, I want to make sure I've dotted my i's and crossed my t's," she added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Rayner also said she wanted was "really clear-eyed on where we were going" with the plans, after Burnham had asked her to look again at the blueprints, which were announced by her predecessor Steve Reed.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson Plans for major overhaul of councils halted Council to take government to court over reforms In her announcement on Monday, Rayner said she was withdrawing plans to reorganise councils in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Those proposals, announced in March, were already subject to legal challenges from Reform-led councils in Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk, and the Conservative-led administration in Hampshire, which were lodged over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also said she wanted to review plans for 16 other areas, including 14 announced by Reed days before Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister and reappointed her to her old role.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Some councils affected by those plans, including Kent and Leicestershire, had threatened similar bids to challenge the lawfulness of the decision-making process.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The government has argued that the plans, which will abolish remaining two-tier areas in England where county and district councils share responsibility for services, would make local government more effective and cost efficient.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: However, critics said the plans would not save money, while diverting resources from front-line services and leaving councils more remote from their communities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Others have also complained that the reorganisation could stymie or delay parallel efforts to merge councils into regional authorities led by mayors, which Burnham has cited as a key part of his economic plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Elsewhere in her interview, Rayner said Labour under Sir Keir should have been quicker to recognise a Palestinian state, having promised to do so as a "contribution to a renewed peace process" at the last election.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Starmer took the move in September last year, having spent much of the prior year  resisting pressure to do so from Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "It's always been Labour policy to recognise a Palestinian state, and it felt like we got there too late.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It was something that should have been really clear," she said.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also denied that UK sanctions against Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, announced on Tuesday , had been made to help Labour ahead of the forthcoming by-election in Holborn and St Pancras in central London.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Pointing to the fact that Western allies had also announced sanctions, she said: "The French and the Canadians are not going to be like 'oh well, we'll just signal something to help you with a local by-election in London'".

sentences.text: Reflecting on her return to government, she said a "big difference" between Burnham and his predecessor in Downing Street was his inclination to tell "the story of why we're doing something" in government.

sentences.text: Colin Sutton was elected as Norfolk's Police and Crime Commissioner two months ago A newly elected £79,000-a-year police commissioner is facing criticism for announcing a 127-date national theatre tour.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: Opposition parties have questioned how Reform UK's Colin Sutton will be able to focus on his job overseeing Norfolk Police, which he was elected to in July.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: The former detective is due to present his true-crime show in theatres across the UK next year discussing police investigations, with tickets priced at around £40.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: Sutton insisted the tour "wouldn't impinge" on his day job, but Labour MP Ben Goldsborough warned "you can't police a county from the back of a tour bus".
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: Labour MP Ben Goldsborough was surprised to learn of the commissioner's tour plan Sutton became one of the UK's most high-profile detectives in the 2000s, leading the investigation to catch serial killer Levi Bellfield , who murdered Milly Dowler, Marsha McDonnell and Amelie Delagrange.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: After retiring from the Metropolitan Police, Sutton wrote a book about the case, which was later turned into an ITV drama .
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: He has also become a regular commentator in the media and last year was named as Reform's national policing and crime advisor.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: In July, after the former Norfolk Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) Sarah Taylor resigned, Sutton comfortably won the election to replace her.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: PCCs are elected officials who set the priorities of a police force, appoint a chief constable and hold them to account.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: This week, promoters of Sutton's "Makings of a Murderer" show announced he was set to tour the country from January to November next year.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: One stretch will see him visit Consett in County Durham, Tamworth in Staffordshire, Hunstanton in Norfolk, Llandudno in north Wales and Leeds over five consecutive nights.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: A drive from venue to venue in that run would cover almost 700 miles (1,126km).
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: "If there is a major incident, you would expect the police and crime commissioner to be there, front and centre," he said.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: "Not operationally, that's down to the chief constable, but in terms of lending his support, communicating with the public, being active and visible." Defending his decision, Sutton said "I spoke to the people around me and we decided that it wouldn't impinge".
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: He continued: "The logistics of each evening are that I turn up at about 7pm, I go on stage at 7.30pm and I'm clear by 10pm.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: "I don't do any rehearsal… I just literally turn up, talk and go away again.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: "The time I'm actually incommunicado is really reduced to the two-hour slots when I'm actually on stage talking.
sentences.article_title: Police boss criticised for 127-date theatre tour

sentences.text: "I'm not a blue light service where I go round and turn up at things." Do you have a story suggestion for Norfolk?

sentences.text: Christopher Harborne (left) and Ben Delo (right) Reform UK has received a second £36m donation in as many days, as cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne matched a record-breaking donation announced late on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Thailand-based Harborne wrote in the Telegraph , external that his "competitive spirit" inspired him to equal Ben Delo's donation - the largest ever given to a UK political party - adding he expected "nothing personally" in return.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Reform said the £72m would be used to hire "the brightest and best minds to work on policy and the most comprehensive plan for government ever".
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The party is facing scrutiny over its finances, as the government seeks to cap donations to UK political parties from British expats.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: There have also been renewed calls by MPs from other political parties for donations from individuals to be capped.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The £72m from the two donations is more than the total received by all UK political parties last year, which stood at just over £69m.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Reform leader Nigel Farage said Harborne and Delo's "generosity" meant the party would "now be able to fight and win the next general election on a level playing field".
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: A Reform UK spokesman added: "We will now also be able to hire up to 400 campaign managers in every target constituency.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: We are now on election footing." The party's deputy leader Richard Tice denied accusations the donations were bad for democracy.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: "It's the opposite actually, we're delighted and very humbled by the confidence expressed by two very successful entrepreneurs who realise Britain's in serious trouble," he told BBC Radio 4's PM programme on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Who is Reform donor and crypto billionaire Ben Delo?
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Reform receives record £36m donation from crypto billionaire Harborne has already donated millions to Reform and Farage, who is currently under investigation by the parliamentary standards commissioner over whether he should have declared a £5m cash gift from Harborne ahead of the 2024 election.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Farage has argued that he was under no obligation to register the "purely private" gift, as it was unrelated to his parliamentary or political activities.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The party is also facing scrutiny after a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week showed two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The Metropolitan Police has said it is investigating, while the party denies any wrongdoing.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The force is also looking into donations given to the party by Fiona Cottrell, mother of longstanding Farage ally George Cottrell, as well as a company controlled by Tice.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Harborne wrote on Saturday that he had "already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life", while Reform was a "start-up party" that lacked "the benefit of hundreds of years of patronage".
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: "A start-up party needs more money than can be provided by membership fees alone, to build and sustain itself and be ready for government," he said.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Harborne and Delo's donations mark the largest sums received by a UK political party since they had to begin declaring them in 2001.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Delo, who also announced his donation in a Telegraph op-ed, said he was giving the money away because he wanted a "fair fight and a level playing field".
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: He said in April he was moving back to Britain from Hong Kong.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: However, the Labour government has introduced a £100,000 cap on donations from British citizens living overseas, and plans to introduce a similar one for those who have recently returned to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: There were nine donations of £1m or more to political parties in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The largest was £9m given to Reform UK by Harborne.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Labour had five donations of £1m or more - totalling nearly £10m - and the Conservatives had three of £1m each.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Labour said Reform and Farage still had "serious questions" to answer about their finances.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said Reform were "drowning" in "sleaze and scandal".
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: She added: "It's time Farage and Reform came clean with the public, fully co-operated with the ongoing police investigations and prove they're not just in it for themselves." Rachel Millward, deputy leader of the Green Party, told BBC News that it wanted a cap on donations from individuals of £500,000.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: She said the donations to Reform were "absolutely staggering amounts", adding:  "What I am very frustrated about is the influence of extreme wealth and the super rich.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: What I want to see is people in politics representing the needs of their communities and ordinary people." Liberal Democrat Cabinet Office spokeswoman Lisa Smart called for the government to introduce emergency legislation to cap donations.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: She said: "These are eye-watering amounts of money.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: This is real emergency for our democracy.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: It presents a very clear and present threat." Labour MP Stella Creasy and other backbenchers had proposed an amendment to the Government's Representation of the People Bill that would stop donors giving parties over £100,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: But the amendment was never debated in the Commons after the government said it would set up a task force to investigate the issue.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The bill will be debated in the House of Lords on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Duncan Hames, director of policy and programmes at campaigning charity Transparency International UK, said: "This is a watershed moment, with two billionaires pledging £72m to one political party in less than 48 hours.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: "This situation is now completely out of control, and makes an irrefutable case for government to bring forward an annual cap on political donations, and fast."
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.article_title: What you need to know about the huge donations to Reform UK

sentences.text: York, pictured, is one of the cities where the regional mayor plans to limit the new levy to 5% of an overnight stay Labour's regional mayors in England have pledged to cap a new fee on visitors' overnight stays at 5%, after hospitality bosses warned it could put jobs at risk.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Local leaders are set to gain new powers to charge an uncapped levy, dubbed a "tourist tax", as a percentage of the cost of hotels, bed and breakfasts and other types of accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: But the Labour mayors in 10 city regions said they would voluntarily limit the charge if they do apply it, adding that they had listened to concerns over costs.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Reform UK's two regional mayors and the two Conservative ones are likely to oppose any levy given criticism from their national parties of the policy.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In a letter to Chancellor John Healey and Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner, the Labour metro mayors said 5% represented a "reasonable ceiling" on the tax.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "It provides a balance of ensuring that local levies are not excessive, or vary significantly between regions, while also leaving room for local variation as appropriate," they added.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: They added this would still allow for "meaningful investment" in local areas, whilst stressing any future levies in their areas would be "subject to local consultation".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The letter was signed by Labour mayors in London, Greater Manchester, Liverpool City Region, West Midlands, North East, West of England, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, East Midlands and York and North Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The government had earlier pledged to protect budget holidays "by making sure low-cost accommodation always pays lowest levy" and said the extra cash could be invested in high streets and local transport.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: While Labour mayors have backed the new levy, others have expressed caution or signalled they will not bring it in.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Local leaders, including heads of Foundation Strategic Authorities where there is no mayor, will need to clarify by early 2028 how the revenue raised should be reinvested.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: They will also be allowed to offer exemptions, such as for campsites.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: However, mayors will not be allowed to exempt whole localities within their regions from the tax, to avoid creating confusion for visitors and businesses.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The government said it would introduce a bill to Parliament "in due course" to bring in the levy, which would apply to both Britons and people visiting from abroad.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Leading trade body UKHospitality has hit back, saying the levy means "jobs are now at risk".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Its chief executive Allen Simpson claimed it would add about £100 to £120 on average to the cost of a family holiday in England, amid fears mayors would make use of the fact there is, in theory, no upper limit for the levy.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "We know, don't we, that local government is struggling for funds - it was hit very hard by austerity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: A 5% tourist tax for overnight stays was introduced in Edinburgh in July The idea was first raised under former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in November and is similar to schemes running in Scotland and European destinations.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Two cities in England already run their own voluntary schemes - a £1 per room, per night City Visitor Charge in Manchester, introduced when Burnham was mayor of the region, and a £2 nightly charge in Liverpool.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: These are business-led schemes where hotels choose to pool the money raised to support local tourism.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Until now, regional mayors have not had the power to bring such fees in themselves - but they argue it is needed to boost economic growth.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Conservative Mayor of Tees Valley Ben Houchen ruled out , external introducing any tourist tax last year.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: John Chappell, who runs five caravan parks in Skegness, Lincolnshire, told BBC Your Voice that many English tourist resorts have visitors on tight budgets already struggling with the cost of car travel.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: He said an extra cost would "kill the industry off".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: "Tourists are the saviours of our resorts, not the demons and ill thought-out ideas like these show how out of touch with reality politicians are," he added.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: The taxes are common in Europe and the rest of the world, with New York, Amsterdam and Rome applying overnight charges to accommodation stays to fund local services.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: However, they are capped in several European cities.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In Scotland local authorities can charge a visitor levy on overnight accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In Edinburgh, the rate is 5% for those staying overnight in hotels, bed and breakfasts and self-catering facilities - capped at five nights.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: It has had a mixed reaction , with some praising extra investment but Scottish Ballet responded by cutting performances while criticising the "unsustainable economics of touring in Edinburgh".
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: In Wales, a capped levy of £1.30 per person per night is set to be introduced in April next year, but it will be up to local authorities to decide whether to roll it out.
sentences.article_title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%

sentences.text: Anthony Lee and his wife Laura pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have pleaded guilty to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: Anthony Lee stood to win approximately £15,000 after placing more than 60 successful bets totalling £1,549, the Gambling Commission said.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: He passed confidential information to his wife about when former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak was planning to call the general election.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: Laura Lee, who was a parliamentary candidate at the time, placed eight successful bets on the election date totalling £535 and would have profited by around £5,000.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: On Thursday at Southwark Crown Court, Anthony Lee pleaded guilty to two offences and Laura Lee pleaded guilty to one offence.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: They will be sentenced in October.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: The trials of 10 other defendants will take place in September 2027 and January 2028.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: Former MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: In Williams' case, the prosecution said he bet £250, £100, and £22.50 on the date of the 2024 election, telling the court he "used highly sensitive and confidential information".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: When details of the scandal first emerged in June 2024, Williams admitted making a "huge error of judgment".
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: Sunak's decision to call the poll was a surprise to many, including many Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: The Conservative Party has been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has denied her party's plans to cut housing benefit would make people homeless, but suggested some would have to "move somewhere cheaper".
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: At Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday, she had challenged Andy Burnham to commit to spending 3% of GDP on defence by 2030, saying the cost could be covered by cuts to welfare.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: The Conservatives have claimed £4bn could be cut from the housing benefit bill, in part by allowing tenancies in areas where housing is expensive to come to an end.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: Asked whether she would be willing to make people homeless in order to fund defence, Badenoch told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the party would "protect existing tenants".
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: During PMQs, Burnham argued national security "can't come at the expense of social security".
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: He repeated that a target date for increasing defence spending to 3% of GDP would be announced in the spending review in the spring.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: The PM insisted he would get the welfare bill down in "the Labour way", by boosting council housebuilding, supporting young people into work and providing more mental health support.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: National security can't come at expense of social security, Burnham says Badenoch accuses Burnham of kicking defence spending into the long grass Badenoch said the government should cut housing benefit to fund defence spending now, adding she would exempt pensioners and existing tenants from the plans.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: Speaking on the Today programme, she said: "What we're doing is making sure that people are protected, but capping the amount that people get on benefits because we need to look after our national security.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: "Without national security, there aren't going to be any benefits.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: Homelessness charity Shelter argued that it was "unrealistic" for families to move to somewhere cheaper as housing benefit rates are set locally.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: "Families would still struggle to find a home they can afford, no matter where they live," added campaigns director Mairi Macrae.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: The Tory proposals would be part of a wider package to increase defending spending to 3% of GDP by 2030, through measures including reimposing the two-child benefit cap.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: The cap, which was scrapped by Labour in April , meant parents could only claim universal credit or tax credits for their first two children.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: Housing benefit can be paid to people who are unemployed or on a low income to help cover the cost of rent.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: The amount someone can claim is linked to the Local Housing Allowance rate, which varies for different council areas.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless

sentences.text: The number of people eligible to claim housing benefit has increased by more than one million since 2020, driven by the soaring cost of private rents.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch denies housing benefit cuts plan would make people homeless
