sentences.text: There could be tens of thousands more teenagers who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) than official statistics suggest, the children's commissioner for England has warned.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: A report by Dame Rachel de Souza said around 42,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England were officially classed as studying at college, but were not showing up at least half of the time.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She said they had gone "under the radar" and were "not getting the support that they need".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said it planned to help colleges track attendance and ultimately to gather that data centrally.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Unlike schools, further education and sixth form colleges in England are not required to collect or report attendance data.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel's report is based on attendance data obtained from 262 college groups in England and says rates are "substantially lower" than in schools.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: It suggests that more than half (52.2%) of 16- and 17-year-olds are estimated to be persistently absent by the standards used in schools, meaning they are missing 10% or more of college sessions.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: And around 42,000 (5.9%) are severely absent, meaning they are missing at least half of college sessions.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The DfE estimates that 57,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England are Neet, and Dame Rachel's report argues that these persistently absent teenagers should be considered as "hidden" Neets alongside them.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel told the BBC a range of factors led to teenagers missing college, including part-time work and travel costs, and that some had been largely absent from education since the Covid pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She said while those juggling part-time employment were likely to miss college every so often, it was those who are "far more vulnerable" who were likely to be severely absent.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She added that it was "shocking" that the DfE did not collect the data as it meant the issue was "ignored".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "It's under the radar and these kids are not getting the support that they need," she said.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: One in eight young people still out of work or education ahead of major review Want your job application to stand out?
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Employers say they look for these six skills Competition for degree apprenticeships quadruples as university costs rise Liam Sloan, principal at Bolton College, said not many students missed more than half of classes, but those who were absent often had mental health challenges or part-time jobs.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "Sometimes the student being able to be offered that £30 shift there and then means more... than the potential qualification in six or seven months' time," he said.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: He said there was a particular issue in English and maths GCSE classes, which students in England are required to study alongside other courses if they don't have a grade 4 or above.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Attendance rates at the college had improved in recent years though, he said, and this year it has introduced full-time "positive engagement officers" to greet students each morning and contact those who do not show up.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: In May, the first instalment of a major report by former minister Alan Milburn warned that figure could be one in six within five years, and that the country was "at risk of a lost generation." The final instalment is expected to set out recommendations for tackling the problem in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel's report describes "hidden" Neets as those enrolled but persistently absent from college, while Milburn's interim report used it to describe those who are Neet and also not claiming benefits, and are therefore harder to reach.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Cath Sezen, director of education policy at the Association of Colleges, said she agreed with many of the report's recommendations but said "funding pressures [were] limiting colleges' ability to provide tailored support".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "We have called time and time again for increased investment, better integration of support services and a stronger national strategy for employer engagement," she said.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The DfE said students in further education needed to be prioritised in future reforms to help tackle the Neets crisis.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: A spokesperson also said a new stepping-stone qualification would be brought in to reduce the "endless treadmill" of students failing and resitting GCSE maths and English, and that the government would track attendance in colleges and accelerate the rollout of mental health support teams.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: English pupils have pulled ahead of the rest of the UK in international reading, maths and science tests, new data suggests, with Scotland and Wales falling further behind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The latest Pisa report, which is published every three years, also warned of a worldwide decline in teenagers' reading skills.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Teenagers were losing the skills that "matter most in the age of AI", such as being able to critically evaluate information from different sources, it said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The share of "hasty readers", who rush through texts to give quick, incorrect answers, has almost doubled between 2018 and 2025.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The report warned the fall was greatest in those from "relatively well off" families.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Run by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the Pisa tests assess teenagers on their ability to solve problems, think critically and communicate, before asking them a wider range of questions about their education in a questionnaire.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Although the UK performed well overall, the rankings varied significantly again, with results showing England, where the curriculum is significantly different, pulling consistently ahead of Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: England's schools minister, Georgia Gould, said the government wanted to "build on" the positive results and "go further so all young people leave school with strong literacy and numeracy".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Pisa tests were taken by a sample of 760,000 15-year-olds in 91 countries.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In the UK, where education differs between the home nations, 15,566 students took the tests in 515 schools.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In England, where it was recently announced that technical subjects would soon be available to students from age 14 , Gould held up high-performing Estonia as an example of where "academic excellence can go hand in hand with high-quality vocational routes".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: "Our reforms will build on England's strong academic foundations so future generations not only perform well, but feel connected to school and excited about where their education can take them," she added.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But Laura Trott, England's shadow education secretary, said the country's successes were down to previous reforms, and accused the new government of trying to "sabotage" them.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Wales falls further behind rest of UK in international school tests Primary teachers hired to teach Glasgow secondary pupils to read While Wales lags behind the rest of the UK overall, on science it is ahead of other European countries such as France, Spain and the Netherlands.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: As the tests last year were taken by 15-year-olds, the results there largely reflect learning under an old curriculum, which has recently been changed.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Anna Brychan, Wales' minister for education and Welsh language, said plans were in place to support schools, adding that the results "highlight our need to improve standards of reading and maths, as a priority".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Scotland's education secretary, Mairi McAllan, said the results showed "real strengths in Scottish education, as well as areas we're already working to improve".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But Scottish Labour said results had "flatlined since 2022's historically poor results", while the Scottish Liberal Democrats said the education system under the SNP had "tumbled down the rankings, lagging behind England on every measure of performance".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's education minister, Paul Givan, said pupils there had performed well by international standards, but that - like other countries - its education system was facing "significant challenges", adding that "there is much more work to do".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Overall, the Pisa tests provide the biggest global snapshot of education systems and an independent view of how teenagers are performing compared with their peers in other countries, so it is a relative measure.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Andreas Schleicher, director of education at the OECD, said reading was the "mother of all skills" and that the steep decline was a concern.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: He said children's ability to read complex texts had declined by the equivalent of "two school years" in the last decade.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Longer-term Pisa research suggested students who read longer books performed best, he added, as it helped them to learn to hold complex information in mind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Schools like Meadow Park, in Coventry, are adopting a range of approaches to improve pupils' reading skills, including weekly book club discussions led by tutors.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Year 10 pupil Ampaabeng said the sessions have had a "really positive impact" on his reading since they were brought in a year ago.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The school has also invested in a wider range of books in the library, where reading for pleasure at lunchtime is encouraged.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: A mobile phone ban was introduced at the school two years ago to reduce distractions - an approach which is commended by the new report.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: "In a digital age, it's easier to pick up a phone than it is a book," head teacher Bernadette Pettman said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: She said reading together had enabled the school to "break down that fear of reading" and that pupils had "absolutely embraced it".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Bernadette Pettman says the school tries to make reading fun with book clubs, creative writing sessions and visits from authors One of the other big changes in education, picked up in the OECD's report, is the use of AI.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: It warns that excessive use can lead to pupils avoiding looking up information themselves, a process sometimes called "cognitive off-loading".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In the UK, the Pisa questionnaire's results suggested a relatively high proportion of teenagers said they had never used AI for their schoolwork.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But the OECD's report said countries were allowing the rapid spread of AI without evidence of its impact, likening it to rolling out an untested vaccine on children.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Schleicher called on governments to provide clear guidelines, and consider whether AI could be used in a targeted way to support teaching rather than to "give quicker answers" to students.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The Lib Dems say schools are approaching an "existential crisis" in teacher retention Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: "The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.
sentences.article_title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The glutinous snail was once widespread in the UK, but is now only found in one Welsh lake A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Ian has about 2,000 of the snails in homemade tanks in his garden Myxas glutinosa gets its name from the gooey mantle that covers its extremely delicate, gold-flecked brown shell.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: It is no bigger than a fingertip, but has comically large antennae - which Hughes likens to "big floppy ears".
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: The snails, which feed on algae and are considered an indicator of healthy lakes and rivers, have been driven to extinction across England.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Polluted water and habitat loss are largely blamed for their disappearance.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Hughes said the snails were "something to preserve and cherish like Egyptian artefacts".
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: The Hughes family are also known for their illustrations of the rare species they have worked to protect In the UK, their last known refuge is Wales' largest natural lake - Llyn Tegid - in Eryri National Park, also known as Snowdonia .
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Since 2014, under licence from Natural Resources Wales, Hughes has been wading into the lake to collect and study the snails.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: He has designed and installed small concrete shelters for them in the lake itself, and set up his own captive population in a greenhouse at his home in Llanarth.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Llyn Tegid is the last known home of the glutinous snail in the UK Hughes was left wondering "will they survive an hour, will they survive a day"?
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Then, after four months, eggs were spotted in the tank.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "Nobody had knowingly seen their eggs before we made that breakthrough," he said.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "You do these things on a wing and a prayer when you're trying to save something that's down to a single site and you're trying to fathom what it needs and how to save it.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: Ian's wife Kerry and their sons Jake, George and Ben, are also fully invested.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "You've got to have a certain mindset to walk out into a freezing cold lake in the middle of January," Ben, 27, explained.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "But knowing that you're helping is more than enough to make it all worth it.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "Every little thing has its place in the ecosystem and if you take a tiny little cog out of any machine it's going to stop working".
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: It is seen as a first step towards restoring them back to locations in the wild over the coming years, as part of a £60m UK government-backed scheme to protect rare species.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "It's such a hugely important conservation project and such a wonderful story," explained Samantha Eden, assistant curator at Wingham Wildlife Park in Kent, who travelled to the Hughes home to pick up 24 glutinous snails.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "We're doing a lot of research on the snails' ecology, their husbandry and their genetics," explained Nicky Needham, head of species management and conservation at BIAZA.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "If we can build up a really strong picture then we're in a good position to reintroduce some of them [to the wild].
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "With fingers and toes crossed I'd like to think that we could achieve that within three years' time." The snails are covered by a 'glutinous' mantle - a layer of translucent tissue that wraps around the shell from beneath.
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: "I think it's an amazing project and we'll support it as much as we can," said Simon Jones, assistant warden at Eryri National Park, who added the park was "really proud" to be home to the "unique species".
sentences.article_title: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK

sentences.text: But climate change means these species are "at an increased threat" and, with the zoos' help, "there's more of a chance of keeping the population alive".

sentences.text: "Having all your eggs in one basket is always a dangerous move so having more experts looking after it is really the right way to go," he said.

sentences.text: AI has increasingly become part of everyday life over the past decade.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The technology takes many forms - from personalising social media feeds to spotting friends in smartphone photos - and accelerating medical breakthroughs.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: But the rise of chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT has prompted concern about the tech's environmental impact, ethical implications and data use.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Recent claims that AI could become too powerful and threaten humanity have also triggered calls for slower development and tighter regulation.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: AI allows computers to process large amounts of data, identify patterns and follow detailed instructions about what to do with that information.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Computers cannot think, empathise or reason.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: However, scientists have developed systems that can perform tasks which usually require human intelligence, trying to replicate how people acquire and use knowledge.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: What is artificial intelligence?
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: This could be trying to anticipate what product an online shopper might buy, based on previous purchases, in order to recommend items.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The technology is also behind voice-controlled virtual assistants like Apple's Siri and Amazon's Alexa, and is being used to develop systems for self-driving cars.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: AI also helps social platforms like Facebook, TikTok and X decide what posts to show users.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Streaming services Spotify and Deezer use AI to suggest music.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: There are also a number of applications in medicine, as scientists use AI to help spot cancers, review X-ray results, speed up diagnoses and identify new treatments.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: A simple guide to help you understand AI Five things you really need to know about AI Generative AI is used to create new content which can seem like it has been made by a human.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: It does this by learning from vast quantities of existing data such as online text and images.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: ChatGPT and Chinese rival DeepSeek's chatbot are popular generative AI tools that can be used to produce text, images, code and more material.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Google's Gemini or Meta AI can similarly hold text conversations with users.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Apps like Midjourney or Veo 3 are dedicated to creating images or video from simple text prompts.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Generative AI can also be used to make high-quality music.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Songs mimicking the style or sound of famous musicians have gone viral , sometimes leaving fans confused about their authenticity.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: How can you tell if your new favourite artist is a real person?
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: While acknowledging AI's potential, some experts are worried about the implications of its rapid growth.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) suggested that AI could affect nearly 40% of jobs , and worsen global financial inequality.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Prof Geoffrey Hinton, a computer scientist regarded as a "godfather" of AI development, warned powerful AI systems could even make humans extinct - although his fear was dismissed by his fellow "AI godfather", Yann LeCun .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: In September 2026 similar fears were raised again after some AI researchers warned the tech could threaten humanity in the near future .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Why are there concerns AI could threaten humanity, and how real are they?
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down But experts have urged a focus on present risks and AI dangers - such as its potential to reproduce biased information, or discriminate against some social groups .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: This is because public data used to train many AI systems can reflect existing societal biases such as sexism or racism.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: And while AI tools are growing more adept, they are still prone to errors.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Generative AI systems are known for their ability to "hallucinate" and assert falsehoods as fact, even sometimes invent sources for inaccurate information.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: In early 2025 Apple pulled an AI feature after it summarised news app notifications incorrectly , and Google also faced criticism for inaccuracies produced by its AI search overviews .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: There are concerns about AI use in schools and workplaces, with students using AI tools to "cheat" on assignments, being wrongly accused of using it and employees "smuggling" it into work .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: But writers, musicians and artists have also pushed back against the tech on ethical grounds.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Many have issued statements or signed open letters accusing AI developers of using their work to train systems without consent or compensation.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Thousands of creators - including Abba singer-songwriter Björn Ulvaeus, writers Ian Rankin and Joanne Harris, and actress Julianne Moore - signed a statement , external in October 2024 calling AI a "major, unjust threat" to their livelihoods.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Billie Eilish is one of many artists who called for an end to "predatory" use of AI in music It is not clear how much energy AI systems use, but some researchers estimate the industry as a whole could soon consume as much as the Netherlands .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Creating the powerful computer chips needed to run AI programmes requires lots of power and water.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Demand for generative AI services has also meant an increase in the number of data centres which power them.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: These huge halls - housing thousands of racks of computer servers - often use substantial amounts of energy or require large volumes of water to keep them cool.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Some large tech companies have invested in ways to reduce or reuse the water needed, or have opted for alternative methods such as air-cooling.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: However, some experts and activists fear that AI will worsen water supply problems.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Beverley Morris flushes her toilet using a bucket because of low water pressure The BBC was told in February that government plans to make the UK a "world leader" in AI could put already stretched supplies of drinking water under strain .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: In September 2024, Google said it would reconsider proposals for a data centre in Chile, which has struggled with drought.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Miliband says climate impact of data centres is uncertain What's the big deal about AI data centres?
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Some governments have already introduced rules governing how AI operates.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The EU's Artificial Intelligence Act places controls on high risk systems used in areas such as education, healthcare, law enforcement or elections.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: It bans some AI use altogether.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Generative AI developers in China are required to safeguard citizens' data, and promote transparency and accuracy of information.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: But they are also bound by the country's strict censorship laws .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Many countries, including the UK, have sought to regulate AI through existing laws rather than legislate - amid concern it could quickly date as AI develops.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The UK has amended laws to target specific AI dangers, such as banning tools that can create deepfake nude imagery or create child sexual abuse material.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: It has also established an independent AI Security Institute to identify risks and evaluate advanced AI models, and signed agreements with the US to collaborate on "robust" AI testing methods.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: But in early 2025, neither country signed a global AI declaration pledging an open, inclusive and sustainable approach to the technology .
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: BBC’s Tom Gerken gets his hands on Valve's Steam Frame Valve's new virtual reality headset, the Steam Frame, has officially been released - but it comes at a high price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The hardware is excellent - a light device which feels comfortable to wear and is packed with clever technology - so long as you're willing to pay a whopping £1,089 for a headset with 1TB of storage.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The variant with 256GB of storage, meanwhile, costs £889.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Both are capable of streaming from a PC as well as playing games on-device, with varying degrees of success.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But it carries a price tag which will make a lot of people roll their eyes, and doesn't do much to dispel criticism that increasingly-costly VR headsets are pricing people out of the hobby.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But before we get into that hefty price tag, is the Steam Frame actually any good?
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: I've owned VR headsets for well over a decade, and Valve's latest effort makes a promising first impression.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Games run well - really the bare minimum considering the price tag - and it's easy enough to use.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Puzzle games like the VR version of Escape Simulator - which tasks you with solving puzzles to exit a room - run great, as you would hope One of the nice things is, like Meta's Quest 3, it has flat "pancake" lenses allowing you to see clearly when you put the headset on.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: It's light - weighing little more than a can of soup.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But what makes it comfortable is the decision to separate the internals up.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The battery pack rests on the back of your head while the screen is at the front - meaning you don't feel front-heavy, a common criticism of other headsets.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But there are better screens out there.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The PlayStation VR2 for example has incredible OLED displays, albeit without the pancake lenses.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Apple and Samsung both have excellent screens too in their own headsets.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Yet these come at a serious premium, costing significantly more than the Steam Frame.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Moss sees you guide a mouse through a series of environments which look excellent in a VR headset - even if a flat screenshot doesn't quite do it justice When Meta launched the Quest 3 in June 2023, its 128GB model retailed for £480.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Less storage, but a much lower price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Three years later, it's hard to believe VR just keeps getting more expensive when the Quest 3 felt like a turning point.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "VR today is ultimately a high-end niche," gaming writer Christopher Dring told me.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "Meta had been subsidising the Quest hardware, and it's difficult to imagine they will going forward as they pivot away from those experiences." Of course, there are reasons for prices going up.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: AI developers are building giant data centres filled with racks of powerful servers, using many of the same components needed to make devices like the Steam Frame.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Ram prices alone more than doubled in price between October 2025 and the start of 2026 .
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the graphics card I bought for £500 a few months ago now sits at closer to £650.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: As prices climb higher and higher, hardware developers don't have much of a choice but to put up their own.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "We set out to come out with a device that would have been much more affordable," Valve developer Jeremy Selan said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "But the global Ram market has impacted us the same way it's impacted everybody." Selan said the firm "fought hard to get it even to this price" and made the decision to ship the Steam Frame despite the price tag The Steam Frame is certainly not a budget product.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But not everyone agrees with the suggestion that VR in general costs too much.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "The idea that it's too expensive is one of the biggest misconceptions about VR," UploadVR website editor David Heaney told me.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: He pointed out while some headsets may be expensive, Meta's Quest 3S budget model costs £320 but has been on sale for £250 several times.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "In context, a Nintendo Switch 2 is £420, an Xbox Series S is £430, and a PS5 is £470 - Quest 3S, which is primarily used for gaming, is cheaper than other games consoles," he said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: He said the big barrier to more people getting into VR was simply that "we're still in the early days".
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "You have to see VR in the same timeframe you'd see personal computers in the 1980s," he said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "Even if they had been cheap, which they weren't, they weren't yet good enough for mainstream adoption.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "VR is only just getting started, a tech in its 1980s PC era, not something anywhere near maturity." What makes the Steam Frame really stand out is its new tech, including what developers call its "foveated streaming".

sentences.text: The tech displays only the exact thing you're looking at in the highest quality, while making things in your peripheral vision less clear.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: You don't notice the low quality bits because you're not looking at them - saving a massive amount of bandwidth.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: It means you can stream VR games wirelessly from your PC in high quality without being tethered by a cable, and it works well.

sentences.text: And it does this while sending two signals at once - combining your household Wi-Fi with a dongle which plugs into your PC.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Valve's Half-Life: Alyx is the most visually stunning game I have played in VR - I've played wireless VR before, but never at this graphical quality when streaming But then again, you need to spend even more money on a decent PC if you want to benefit from that - which doesn't help with concerns about price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Valve says despite it being a VR headset, the Steam Frame is not just for VR games.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Selan told me the hope is people will also use it to play their non-VR games too, using the headset as a screen.

sentences.text: But it's an interesting thought - and I'd love to be proven wrong.

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
